newsitem.title: UK: LPC - Dartford & Gravesham plan debt syndication.
newsitem.headline: LPC - Dartford & Gravesham plan debt syndication.

text.p: LONDON, July 31 (LPC) - The 143 million stg private financing initiative (PFI) hospital project for the Dartford & Gravesham National Health Service Trust is now fully financed, and 108 million stg of senior debt facilities are being readied for general syndication.
The deal is the first PFI hospital project to reach financial completion, and has been delayed by the resolution of a number of technical issues common to all PFI projects in the NHS.

The transactions have been delayed by the enactment of the vires bill, which clarifies the legal powers of trusts to enter into PFI agreements, and other issues such as termination on default, and the definition and consequence of force majeure.

Commercial close of the project, which backs the construction of a new 400-bed hospital on a greenfield site at Darenth Park, was reached in February. However, the conditions -- government approval of the scheme, financial close and planning consent -- have now been met and the transaction has been declared unconditional.
The senior debt is being arranged by Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Rabobank and United Bank of Kuwait, and will reach the market next month.

The hospital will be built by The Hospital Company (THC), a PFI bidding team comprised of Tarmac Group and United Medical Enterprises. THC has assumed construction and delay risk, and service performance risk during the operational phase.
